title: fix(update): repair refuses forever when a plugin changed after the update
body:
Related: #193132

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: `openclaw update repair` fails on every attempt when a plugin's data/settings obligation or install record changed after an update published it.

## User Impact

User impact: repair now finishes the plugin rollback instead of refusing forever. It keeps the newer change, restores everything else, and reports what it kept as a warning. The warning shows in repair output, in `openclaw doctor` under update history, and in the update report.

## Why This Change Was Made

When rollback found a plugin migration obligation or install record that matched neither the update's original value nor what the update wrote, it threw. That throw happened before anything was written, so the newer value survived either way. The only effect was that the cohort could never settle. Repair, Doctor and triage then kept pointing at each other, and the cohort pinned capture and rollback artifacts indefinitely.

Rollback now keeps that newer value, skips it, restores every item that still matches, and completes. `restorePluginCohortMigrationRowsInDatabase` returns the plugins it kept. `settleUpdatePluginCohort` collects those along with any install records it kept, and writes one `warning:plugin-cohort:later-changes-kept` step on the update run. Doctor and the run report already show completed warning steps. A kept install record also keeps its source snapshot, so the record and snapshot can't disagree.

One related refusal goes the same way. If the obligation table itself is gone, because the database was restored from a backup older than it, rollback no longer refuses. It now leaves that state alone instead of initializing the candidate schema, and reports the original obligations as kept.

The settlement result shape is unchanged, so the worker callers' strict result parsing still holds. Commit does not restore anything and is unaffected. The live updater rollback still rechecks the database before it restores the previous package. Repair's ordering doesn't need to change: once rollback can't refuse, repair no longer gets stuck settling the cohort before package recovery runs.

Three refusals are left for a follow-up: published artifacts that changed, config files edited after publication, and a source snapshot that changed while its install record did not. Corrupt publication chains still refuse, because that is a journal integrity failure rather than a later writer.

## Evidence

Red on base `480d50305383`, using real SQLite and the real install index:

- `src/infra/update-plugin-cohort-recovery.test.ts`: the later-Doctor-decision case, in both baseline variants, fails with "Plugin migration obligation changed after update publication". The older-backup case fails with "Plugin migration recovery is missing its original obligations". The two other older-database cases fail only on the new return value.
- `src/plugins/update-cohort-recovery.test.ts`: the new later-install-record case fails with "Plugin fixture changed after the update; cohort recovery preserved it."

Green on head:

- Both files pass (16 and 17 tests).
- The later obligation and the later install record are kept.
- In the same rollback, a matching install record for a second plugin is restored, which is the negative control. The earlier steps of the migration test also restore matching rows.
- The cohort is deleted, and the update run's warning projection contains the recorded warning.
- The existing record-conflict test is rewritten to this outcome rather than deleted. Its artifact and chain cases still refuse.

`node scripts/test-projects.mts` across the two files above, plus `src/plugins/update-cohort.test.ts`, `src/cli/update-cli/update-repair-command.test.ts`, `src/cli/update-cli/update-repair-handoff.test.ts`, `src/cli/update-cli/update-command-plugin-cohort-handoff.test.ts`, `src/infra/update-plugin-cohort-commit.process.test.ts` and `src/cli/update-cli/update-command-database-rollback.test.ts`: 127 passed.

Format check passes, `lint:core` has no findings in the touched files, and the import cycle check is clean. Locally, `tsrs` on core and the infra, plugins-platform and cli-update test shards shows only the existing `packages/ai` error that base also has. The test-line allocation matches the 260 lines this branch adds against current main.



After #193132 merged, I merged main into this branch. Repair's forward settlement and best-effort rollback now share `settleUpdatePluginCohort`, and rollback uses the action that settlement resolved. The repair settlement tests in `src/cli/update-cli/update-plugin-cohort-settlement.test.ts` that used to expect a refusal ("keeps rollback selected") now check that rollback completes, the later decision is kept, and the kept-change warning is recorded. The forward cases check that no warning is recorded, so the two paths stay distinguishable. All 11 cases pass. The related suites, including the cohort and repair tests above, pass with 138 tests.


Review follow-up:

- **Installation owner keys.** Install records are keyed by installation owner, and source snapshots by plugin ID. Keeping a later `package-owner` record used to leave the `demo` plugin's snapshot restoration queued. The installed-index owner then rejected it ("Plugin demo source snapshot changed after the update"). A kept installation now drops every snapshot restoration whose recorded install owner is that key. It falls back to the plugin ID only when no owner is recorded. New test in `src/plugins/update-cohort-recovery.test.ts`, using the `demo` / `package-owner` shape: red with that error before the fix, green after (18/18).
- **Stored data compatibility.** The new last case in `src/cli/update-cli/update-plugin-cohort-settlement.test.ts` writes the update recovery and plugin cohort rows into real SQLite exactly as shipped updaters and the refused repair stored them on the affected install: disposition `rollback`, revision 2, `settledPublications: 0`, and one `plugin-migrations` publication for discord and whatsapp. Only paths and the run identity differ. It then repairs with this branch's code. The rows load without migration, rollback completes, both later obligations stay as they are, recovery admission clears, and the warning names both plugins. Run against current main's source, the same stored rows load and then refuse with "Plugin migration obligation changed after update publication: discord". This PR adds no stored field, so released rows keep the same shape.
- **Docs.** `docs/install/updating.md` now describes the new outcome in the npm plugin rollback section. Later install-record and obligation changes are kept, rollback completes, and an update warning names them. Settings and artifacts still leave recovery unfinished in this PR; #193645 covers those.
- **Checks.** Related suites pass with 150 tests across 10 files, including the installed-index snapshot tests. Format, the docs MDX check and `tsrs` (apart from the existing `packages/ai` error) are clean. Autoreview at P2 is clean.
